title: Garbha Khel
subtitle: 12 joyful activities for mother & baby — play, paint, listen, repeat

activities.title: Colour a Mandala
steps: Put on the music. Pick 3 colours only.
Colour from the centre outwards, one ring per song.
Breathe slowly; tell baby which colour you chose.
activities.music: Raga Yaman on bansuri — Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia (evening)

spirit.meaning: That is whole, this is whole — you are whole, and so is your baby.

activities.baby: Calm music and your relaxed heartbeat and breathing reach baby; from ~19 weeks baby hears low tones.
activities.mom: Focused, repetitive colouring lowered anxiety in studies; it rests the busy mind.

activities.title: Śrī Yantra Gaze & Trace
steps: Light a diya. Look softly at the red dot (bindu) for 1 minute — blink freely.
Chant Oṃ 3 times on long, easy out-breaths.
Trace one triangle with your finger or pencil each time.

spirit.meaning: The lamp’s light brings goodness, wellbeing and health — I bow to that light.

activities.baby: Slow, humming exhalations calm your body; baby feels your steady rhythm.
activities.mom: A single point of focus quiets racing thoughts — a traditional meditation aid.

activities.title: Kolam Dot Game
steps: Trace the sample loop with one unbroken line.
Game: on the empty grid, make your own loop without lifting the pencil.
Next time, try a bigger loop. Smile at every wobble.

spirit.meaning: May all be happy. (Rice-flour kolams traditionally feed ants and birds — kindness to every being.)

activities.baby: Your relaxed, absorbed state means calmer stress hormones for both of you.
activities.mom: A gentle puzzle for hand and eye — attention, patience and a small win every time.

activities.title: Kick-and-Tap Game
steps: Lie on your side when baby is active. Hands on your belly.
When baby kicks, gently tap or stroke that spot and say ‘Hello!’
Wait. Did baby kick back? Tally the replies below — a game you share.
activities.music: Your own humming of the family lullaby

spirit.iast: saha nāv avatu | saha nau bhunaktu |
spirit.meaning: May we two be protected together; may we be nourished together.

activities.baby: In a 4D-scan study, babies moved more when mothers stroked their belly — touch is baby’s first language.
activities.mom: Joyful connection; you learn your baby’s pattern (call your doctor if movements slow down).

activities.title: One Lullaby, Every Night
steps: Choose ONE lullaby (any language you love).
Sing it softly every night — same song, same time.
After birth, sing it when baby cries: it may sound like home.
activities.music: Sing yourself. Ideas: Omanathinkal Kidavo · Jo Achyutananda · Chanda Mama · Brahms’ Lullaby

spirit.meaning: You are pure, you are awake, you are spotless — Queen Madālasā’s lullaby.

activities.baby: Newborns show memory for melodies and voices heard often before birth (Partanen 2013).
activities.mom: Singing slows and deepens breathing; it builds your bond and confidence.

activities.title: Story with Voices
steps: Read the mini-story aloud, with a monkey voice and a crocodile voice.
Game: retell it from memory next time — add one new detail.
Ask: ‘What would you do, little one?’
activities.music: No music — your voice is the music

spirit.meaning: The whole world is one family. (Hitopadeśa / Mahā Upaniṣad)

activities.baby: Your voice is the clearest sound in the womb; newborns recognise stories read to them often (DeCasper 1986).
activities.mom: Playful voices and recall keep your mind lively and lighten the mood.

activities.title: Paint Your Feelings
steps: Close your eyes: what colour is today’s feeling?
Paint or finger-paint it in the frame — shapes, swirls, no rules.
Add one bright colour for a wish for baby. Date it.
activities.music: Santoor — ‘Call of the Valley’, Pt. Shivkumar Sharma

spirit.meaning: Lead me from darkness to light.

activities.baby: Releasing worries lowers your stress — the environment baby grows in.
activities.mom: Art-making reduces stress in many studies; naming feelings softens them.

activities.title: Belly Art & Photo
steps: Partner draws a lotus, moon or sun on the bump — natural henna or body-safe washable paint.
Play music and talk to baby while you draw.
Take a photo; stick a print in the frame on the last page.

spirit.meaning: Salutations to Gaṇeśa, remover of obstacles — said before every auspicious beginning.

activities.baby: Gentle touch on the belly draws baby’s responses; partner’s voice becomes familiar too.
activities.mom: Laughter, touch and care from your partner — oxytocin, the calm-and-connect hormone.

activities.title: Humming Bee Breath
steps: Sit tall. Touch thumb and index finger (Jñāna mudrā).
Breathe in through the nose; breathe out humming ‘mmm’ like a bee.
7 rounds — never hold the breath. Then sit in silence for one minute.
activities.music: Silence — then a temple bell or conch to finish
activities.baby: Humming vibration and slow breath settle your nervous system; baby hears the low hum.
activities.mom: Long humming out-breaths shift the body towards ‘rest and digest’ (small studies).

activities.title: Name-That-Raga Game
steps: Partner plays a 30-second clip — flute, veena, sitar, bells, conch, or a raga.
Guess the instrument or raga. 1 point each!
Keep score below. Winner chooses tonight’s lullaby.
activities.music: Mix: Bhairav (morning), Bhoopali, Desh, Yaman (evening), Malkauns (night)

spirit.meaning: Sound is the divine — music as a path to stillness.

activities.baby: Baby hears a rich variety of melodies and rhythms at a comfortable volume.
activities.mom: A playful listening game: attention, memory and plenty of laughter.

activities.title: Gratitude Garland
steps: Each day, colour one flower on the garland.
Say aloud one thing you are grateful for today.
When the garland is full, read it to baby — and start a new one.

spirit.meaning: May the divine light inspire our minds. (Gāyatrī mantra, Ṛgveda 3.62.10)

activities.baby: Positive mood in pregnancy is linked with calmer stress responses.
activities.mom: Daily gratitude gives small, lasting boosts to wellbeing.

activities.title: Moonlight Sway
steps: Evening: put on slow music, hold your partner or a chair.
Sway side to side like a cradle — slow, small, smooth. No jumping or spinning.
End by looking at the moon and telling baby its shape tonight.
activities.music: Raga Bageshri or a slow garba; a cradle song (hālaraḍuṃ)

spirit.meaning: White as curd, conch and snow, born of the milky ocean — salutations to the Moon. (Navagraha stotra)

activities.baby: Rhythmic rocking is how babies are soothed — baby already feels your gentle movement.
activities.mom: Gentle movement eases the back, lifts mood and helps sleep.

playlist: Raga Bhairav / Ahir Bhairav · Venkatesa Suprabhatam (M.S. Subbulakshmi)
Raga Bhimpalasi · santoor ‘Call of the Valley’ (Shivkumar Sharma & Hariprasad Chaurasia)
Raga Yaman on bansuri · Raga Bhoopali · veena Raga Mohanam
Raga Bageshri / Malkauns · your family lullaby · tanpura drone
Om chanting · Bhaja Govindam · Kurai Ondrum Illai · nature sounds (rain, birds)

eat: ragi, poha, greens, dates + amla, lemon
habits: Sleep 7–9 hours; from 28 weeks go to sleep on your side.
Walk 20–30 minutes most days (as your doctor allows).
Take the folic acid, iron and calcium your doctor prescribes.
No alcohol or tobacco; under 200 mg caffeine a day; only boiled/pasteurised milk; fully cooked eggs and meat.
basics.warn: Call your doctor at once for bleeding, fluid leaking, baby moving less, severe headache or blurred vision, swelling of face/hands, fever, severe pain, or feeling unable to cope. Ambulance 108 · Tele-MANAS 14416.
